turn1.explanation: The unit fires on the last token of a line, the token immediately before a newline, whatever that token is (punctuation, word, number, brace). It is strongest in code, config and license headers, and somewhat weaker at line ends in prose, lists and headings.
turn1.evidence: Every marked token ends its line: YAML values (' 1', ' 0'), Apache license line ends ('2.0', ' software', 'BASIS,'), the code token '{', 'aCoder', 'info' and ';' before a line break, the Jung quote's last word 'Book', and the '* *' separator. The mid-range examples follow the same pattern with surnames ending list lines, '}' after section anchors, ' Invention', ' read', and sentence-final '.' before a newline.
turn1.missing_data: Activations on text with no line breaks would test whether the trigger is really the newline. Activation on the newline token itself and on tokens at the end of very long lines would also help, as would a test of whether code versus prose explains the strength difference.
